correctness.rationale: For \(m=1\), the geometric log-PGF has positive coefficients \(q^k/k\). For \(m=2\), the exact PGF is \((1-q)^2(1+qz)/((1-qz)(1-q^2z))\), whose logarithm yields strictly positive summable compound-Poisson jump coefficients. For every integer \(m\ge3\), write \(u=1+q\), \(v=1+q+q^2\). The identity \(u^6+1-2v^3=q^2(3+6q+3q^2-q^4)>0\), followed by Jensen convexity of \(x^{m/3}\), gives \(v^m<(u^{2m}+1)/2\) and hence a strictly negative quadratic log-PGF coefficient. The analytic proof covers all parameters. Finite exact-rational tests are supplementary.
